title: The central GJ 433 outer orbit leaks less than 0.28 m/s into a fixed 35.23-day fit with a quadratic trend
abstract: We test whether a long orbit can cause a selected 35.23-day residual in 86 public GJ 433 HARPS exposures. Exact Kepler orbits are projected through a quadratic fit and two known-period waves. With the published central outer-orbit period of 5094.105 days, eccentricity 0.12 and semi-amplitude 1.75 m/s, an analytic phase-grid bound limits leakage to 0.274145 m/s for all phases and directions of periastron. The observed fitted residual amplitude is 2.296780 m/s. The central orbit alone cannot cause that amplitude in this fit. A numerical search over a wider hypothetical range reaches 2.332 m/s at semi-amplitude 5 m/s, so an amplitude argument does not exclude all outer-orbit error. Five controls retain the central-orbit mismatch. Wide-range search peaks are not certified upper limits and need not fit the full velocity curve. Fixed short periods, unknown activity noise, no joint orbit posterior and no new independent observations limit inference. No new planet is found. Code, aggregate results, a figure and external retrieval steps support reproduction.

display.caption: The central orbit gives small leakage relative to each fitted residual amplitude. Wider hypothetical ranges give numerical search peaks of comparable size in some fits. They are not certified upper limits or fits to the full velocity curve.

citations.reason: Provides the selected residual and the open test of long-orbit trend error. We add an exact-orbit leakage calculation with new code.
